idea.body: Factoring pulls the piece every term shares back out to the front. 6x + 15 has terms that share a factor of 3, so it factors as 3(2x + 5). Check it by multiplying back: 3 times 2x is 6x, and 3 times 5 is 15. A four-term expression sometimes has no single shared factor, but grouping still works. Pull a factor from the first two terms, and a separate factor from the last two terms. If the two leftover binomials match, pull that shared binomial out too. An area model shows the same idea as a rectangle split back into its side lengths.

figure.alt: An area model splitting 6x + 15 into a 3 by (2x + 5) rectangle.

steps: Find the greatest common factor of all three terms: 4.
Divide each term by 4: x^2, 2x, and 3.
Write the factor out front and the rest inside parentheses: 4(x^2 + 2x + 3).
Check by multiplying back: 4 times x^2 is 4x^2, 4 times 2x is 8x, and 4 times 3 is 12.

figure.alt: An area model splitting 4x^2 + 8x + 12 into a 4 by (x^2 + 2x + 3) rectangle.

ways.name: Pull out the greatest common factor
ways.when: Use this default method whenever every term shares a common factor.
steps: Find the greatest common factor of 9 and 21: it is 3.
Divide each term by 3: 9x divided by 3 is 3x, and 21 divided by 3 is 7.
Write the factor out front and the rest inside parentheses: 3(3x + 7).
Check by multiplying back: 3 times 3x is 9x, and 3 times 7 is 21.
ways.trap: Pulling out a common factor that is not the greatest one, leaving more to factor.

ways.name: Group in pairs
ways.when: Use this when four terms have no single factor shared by all of them.
steps: Split the four terms into two pairs: (x^3 + 3x^2) and (2x + 6).
Pull the common factor from the first pair: x^2(x + 3).
Pull the common factor from the second pair: 2(x + 3).
Both pairs share the binomial (x + 3), so pull that out too.
ways.trap: Pairing terms that leave no matching binomial, so the shared bracket never appears.

ways.name: The area model in reverse
ways.when: Use this to see factoring as finding a rectangle's missing side.
steps: Picture 8x + 20 as the total area of a rectangle.
One side length is the greatest common factor, 4.
Divide the area by that side: 8x divided by 4 is 2x, 20 divided by 4 is 5.
ways.trap: Guessing the missing side length instead of dividing the area by the known side.

figure.alt: An area model splitting 8x + 20 into a 4 by (2x + 5) rectangle, each box labelled with its product.

stretch.prompt: What is the greatest common factor of 84 and 126?
explanation: Break both numbers into their prime factors.
84 = 2^2 times 3 times 7, and 126 = 2 times 3^2 times 7.
The shared primes multiply to 42.

Multiply only the primes both numbers share, using the smaller power of each.
